questions.question: Congo was named by Europeans. Congo's dictator Mobuto later changed the name of the country and the river to Zaire with the objective of Africanising names of persons and spaces. However, the name Zaire was a Portuguese alteration of Nzadi o Nzere, a local African term meaning `River that swallows Rivers'. Zaire was the Portuguese name for the Congo river in the 16th and 17th centuries. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the paragraph above?
options: Mobuto was not entirely successful in Africanising the name of his country
The term Nzadi o Nzere was of Portuguese origin
Mobuto's desire to Africanise names was prevented by the Portuguese
As a dictator Mobuto ordered the Portuguese to alter the name of the river to Zaire
questions.explanation:
As the paragraph states, dictator Mobuto wanted to Africanise the name of Congo but could not fully succeed, as the new name ``Zaire'' given to the country was itself a Portuguese alteration of the local African term Nzadi o Nzere.
  • Option (a): The replacement name was still of Portuguese origin, so Africanisation was not entirely successful — TRUE (inferable).
  • Option (b): Nzadi o Nzere is a local African term, not Portuguese — FALSE.
  • Option (c): Portuguese did not prevent Mobuto — FALSE.
  • Option (d): Mobuto changed the name himself; he did not order the Portuguese — FALSE.
\[\boxed{\text{A) Mobuto was not entirely successful in Africanising the name of his country}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: M and N had four children P, Q, R and S. Of them, only P and R were married. They had children X and Y respectively. If Y is a legitimate child of W, which one of the following statements is necessarily FALSE?
options: M is the grandmother of Y
R is the father of Y
W is the wife of R
W is the wife of P
questions.explanation:
From the family tree: \[M - N \longrightarrow P,\; Q,\; R-W,\; S\] \[P \longrightarrow X, \qquad R \longrightarrow Y\] Analysing each statement:
  • \(W\) can't be wife of \(P\) — \(P\) is already married to someone else (has child \(X\)); \(W\) is married to \(R\). (Necessarily FALSE)
  • \(W\) can be husband or wife of \(R\) (gender not specified for \(R\)).
  • \(R\) can be father or mother of \(Y\).
  • \(M\) can be grandfather of \(Y\).
\[\boxed{\text{D) } W \text{ is the wife of } P}\]
Key points
  • \(Y\) is a legitimate child of \(W\), so \(W\) is the spouse of \(R\) (parent of \(Y\)).
  • Since \(W\) is married to \(R\), \(W\) cannot simultaneously be the wife of \(P\).
  • Gender of \(R\) and \(W\) is not specified, so other options remain possible.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Once the team of analysts identify the problem, we _____ in a better position to comment on the issue. Which one of the following choices CANNOT fill the given blank?
questions.explanation:
The first clause ``Once the team of analysts identify the problem'' is in the simple present tense. The second clause must therefore use a present or future form — not a past tense form.
  • (a) will be — simple future; grammatically consistent.
  • (b) were to be — past subjunctive; clashes with the present tense of the first clause. \(\checkmark\) Cannot fill.
  • (c) are going to be — present future; grammatically consistent.
  • (d) might be — modal (present/future possibility); grammatically consistent.
\[\boxed{\text{(B) were to be }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A final examination is the ___________ of a series of evaluations that a student has to go through.
questions.explanation:
A ``final examination'' represents the last and highest point in a series of evaluations — i.e., the endpoint of the entire evaluation process.
  • Insinuation — an indirect hint or suggestion; unrelated.
  • Desperation — a state of hopelessness; unrelated.
  • Culmination — the final result or highest point of a progressive series. \(\checkmark\)
  • Consultation — a discussion or meeting; unrelated.
\[\boxed{\text{(A) Culmination }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Are there enough seats here? There are _____ people here than I expected.
questions.explanation:
The blank requires a comparative degree adjective because the sentence signals a comparison using the word than.
  • ``most'' and ``least'' are superlative forms — used when comparing three or more items without ``than''.
  • ``many'' is a positive-degree adjective — no comparison implied.
  • ``more'' is the comparative form of ``many/much'' and pairs correctly with ``than''.
\[\boxed{\text{(D) More }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: While teaching a creative writing class in India, I was surprised at receiving stories from the students that were all set in distant places: in the American West with cowboys and in Manhattan penthouses with clinking ice cubes. This was, till an eminent Caribbean writer gave the writers in the once-colonised countries the confidence to see the shabby lives around them as worthy of being ``told''. The writer of this passage is surprised by the creative writing assignments of his students, because ___________.
options: Some of the students had written stories set in foreign places
None of the students had written stories set in India
None of the students had written about ice cubes and cowboys
Some of the students had written about ice cubes and cowboys
questions.explanation:
The passage describes a creative writing teacher in India who was surprised to receive stories from students that were all set in distant, foreign places (the American West, Manhattan penthouses) — none of them set in India or in the students' immediate surroundings.
  • (a) Incorrect — writing stories set in foreign places is exactly what happened; the surprise is that no story was set locally in India.
  • (b) Correct — the teacher was surprised precisely because none of the students had written stories set in India; all stories were set in distant, foreign locales. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) Incorrect — ice cubes and cowboys are mentioned as settings; students had written about them.
  • (d) Incorrect — some students did write about ice cubes and cowboys; this is not the source of surprise.
\[\boxed{\text{(b) None of the students had written stories set in India.}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: X is an online media provider. By offering unlimited and exclusive online content at attractive prices for a loyalty membership, X is almost forcing its customers towards its loyalty membership. If its loyalty membership continues to grow at its current rate, within the next eight years more households will be watching X than cable television. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the above paragraph?
options: Most households that subscribe to X's loyalty membership discontinue watching cable television
Non-members prefer to watch cable television
Cable television operators don't subscribe to X's loyalty membership
The X is cancelling accounts of non-members
questions.explanation:
The passage states that X offers unlimited and exclusive online content at attractive prices, almost forcing customers toward its loyalty membership, and that its membership base continues to grow. Within eight years, more households will watch X than cable television.
  • (a) If subscribers of X will outnumber cable TV subscribers, the most natural inference is that households subscribing to X discontinue watching cable television — this is the underlying assumption driving the projection. \(\checkmark\)
  • (b) Non-members preferring cable TV is not stated; the passage focuses on loyalty-membership subscribers.
  • (c) The passage makes no claim about the behaviour of cable operators; cannot be inferred.
  • (d) Cancelling accounts of non-members is not mentioned or implied.
\[\boxed{\text{(A) Most households that subscribe to X’s loyalty mem- bership discontinue watching cable television }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The search engine's business model _____ around the fulcrum of trust.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires a verb meaning to have something as its central or pivotal focus. The noun fulcrum denotes the central support point of a lever — metaphorically, the most essential element of an activity.
  • (a) revolves — ``revolves around'' means to have something as its central theme or pivot. \(\checkmark\)
  • (b) plays — ``plays around'' implies casual behaviour; does not convey centrality.
  • (c) sinks — implies collapse or descent; contextually inappropriate.
  • (d) bursts — implies sudden breaking apart; contextually inappropriate.
\[\boxed {\text{A) revolves}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A court is to a judge as _____ is to a teacher.
questions.explanation:
The analogy tests the workplace relationship: a court is the place where a judge works; similarly, a school is the place where a teacher works.
  • (a) a student — a student is taught by a teacher, not the place of work.
  • (b) a punishment — unrelated to the workplace analogy.
  • (c) a syllabus — related to teaching content, not a place; does not complete the analogy.
  • (d) a school — a school is the workplace of a teacher, exactly mirroring court : judge. \(\checkmark\)
\[\text{Court} : \text{Judge} \;\;=\;\; \text{School} : \text{Teacher}\] \[\boxed{ \text{ D) A School}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
The police arrested four criminals -- P, Q, R and S. The criminals knew each other. They made the following statements:
  • P says ``Q committed the crime.''
  • Q says ``S committed the crime.''
  • R says ``I did not do it.''
  • S says ``What Q said about me is false.''
Assume only one of the arrested four committed the crime and only one of the statements made above is true. Who committed the crime?
questions.explanation:
Let C denote ``criminal'' and NC denote ``not criminal''. Exactly one person committed the crime and exactly one statement is true. We test each case by assuming exactly one statement is true (T) and the rest false (F). The four statements are:
  • P says: ``Q committed the crime.''
  • Q says: ``S committed the crime.''
  • R says: ``I did not do it.''
  • S says: ``What Q said about me is false.''
Case I — Only P's statement is true:
CriminalsPQRS
AssumptionTFFF
Result\(Q_{\text{C}}\)\(S_{\text{NC}}\)\(R_{\text{C}}\)\(S_{\text{C}}\)
\(Q_{\text{C}}\) and \(R_{\text{C}}\) both criminal \(\Rightarrow\) impossible (only one person committed the crime). Case II — Only Q's statement is true:
CriminalsPQRS
AssumptionFTFF
Result\(Q_{\text{NC}}\)\(S_{\text{C}}\)\(R_{\text{C}}\)\(S_{\text{C}}\)
\(S_{\text{C}}\) and \(R_{\text{C}}\) both criminal \(\Rightarrow\) impossible. Case III — Only R's statement is true:
CriminalsPQRS
AssumptionFFTF
Result\(Q_{\text{NC}}\)\(S_{\text{NC}}\)\(R_{\text{NC}}\)\(S_{\text{C}}\)
\(S_{\text{NC}}\) and \(S_{\text{C}}\) simultaneously \(\Rightarrow\) contradiction (S is both criminal and not criminal). Case IV — Only S's statement is true:
CriminalsPQRS
AssumptionFFFT
Result\(Q_{\text{NC}}\)\(S_{\text{NC}}\)\(R_{\text{C}}\)\(S_{\text{NC}}\)
Only \(R_{\text{C}}\) — exactly one criminal, no contradictions. This case is consistent. \(\checkmark\) \[\boxed{ \text{ B) S}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: "A recent High Court judgement has sought to dispel the idea of begging as a disease --- which leads to its stigmatization and criminalization --- and to regard it as a symptom. The underlying disease is the failure of the state to protect citizens who fall through the social security net." Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?
options: Beggars are lazy people who beg because they are unwilling to work
Beggars are created because of the lack of social welfare schemes
Begging is an offence that has to be dealt with firmly
Begging has to be banned because it adversely affects the welfare of the state
questions.explanation:
The passage argues that begging should be viewed as a symptom rather than a disease, and that the true underlying disease is the failure of the state to protect citizens who fall through the social security net.
  • (a) The passage explicitly opposes criminalisation of begging; treating it as an offence to be ``dealt with firmly'' contradicts the passage.
  • (b) The passage states that the underlying cause of begging is the failure of social welfare/security mechanisms, directly implying that beggars are created by the lack of adequate social welfare schemes. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) The passage does not suggest banning begging; it argues against stigmatisation and criminalisation.
  • (d) Characterising beggars as lazy is a moral judgement not supported anywhere in the passage.
\[\boxed{ \text{ B) Beggars are created because of the lack of social welfare schemes}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Three of the five students allocated to a hostel put in special requests to the warden. Given the floor plan of the vacant rooms, select the allocation plan that will accommodate all their requests. Request by X: Due to pollen allergy, I want to avoid a wing next to the garden. Request by Y: I want to live as far from the washrooms as possible, since I am very sensitive to smell. Request by Z: I believe in Vaastu and so want to stay in the South-west wing. The shaded rooms are already occupied. WR is washroom.
questions.explanation:
The three requests impose the following constraints:
  • X — pollen allergy; must be placed in a room not adjacent to the garden.
  • Y — sensitive to smell; must be placed as far from the washrooms (WR) as possible.
  • Z — Vaastu; must be placed in the South-West (SW) wing.
Evaluating each option against all three constraints:
  • (a) Y is close to WR \(\Rightarrow\) violates Y's constraint.
  • (b) X is placed next to the garden \(\Rightarrow\) violates X's constraint.
  • (c) Z is not in the SW wing \(\Rightarrow\) violates Z's constraint.
  • (d) X is away from the garden; Y is farthest from WR; Z is in the SW wing. All three constraints satisfied. \(\checkmark\)

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The fishermen, ______ the flood victims owed their lives, were rewarded by the government.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires a relative pronoun introducing a clause that modifies ``the fishermen'' (a person) and functions as the object of the preposition ``to'' (i.e. the flood victims owed their lives to the fishermen).
  • (a) whom — refers to a person but lacks the preposition to; incomplete prepositional relationship.
  • (b) to which — which refers to things, not people.
  • (c) to whom — whom refers to persons; to whom correctly completes ``owed their lives to whom''. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) that — that cannot follow preposition directly in formal, and does not suit the person reference here.
\[\boxed{ \text{ C) to whom}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
Some students were not involved in the strike. If the above statement is true, which of the following conclusions is/are logically necessary?
  1. Some who were involved in the strike were students.
  2. No student was involved in the strike.
  3. At least one student was involved in the strike.
  4. Some who were not involved in the strike were students.
questions.explanation:
Given statement: ``Some students were not involved in the strike.'' This means the set of Students and the set of Strike-participants partially overlap — some students are inside the strike circle, some are outside. Evaluating each conclusion:
  1. Some who were involved in the strike were students.
    The diagram allows this but does not guarantee it — the strike circle could lie entirely outside the student circle. Not necessary.
  2. No student was involved in the strike.
    Contradicts the premise (which only says some were not involved; others may have been). Not necessary.
  3. At least one student was involved in the strike.
    The premise only confirms some students were not involved — it does not confirm any were involved. Not necessary.
  4. Some who were not involved in the strike were students.
    This is a direct restatement of the premise. Logically necessary. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{(c) only 4}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Until Iran came along, India had never been ______ in kabaddi.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Since the last one year, after a 125 basis point reduction in repo rate by the Reserve Bank of India, banking institutions have been making a demand to reduce interest rates on small saving schemes. Finally, the government announced yesterday a reduction in interest rates on small saving schemes to bring them on par with fixed deposit interest rates. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?
options: Whenever the Reserve Bank of India reduces the repo rate, the interest rates on small saving schemes are also reduced
Interest rates on small saving schemes are always maintained on par with fixed deposit interest rates
The government sometimes takes into consideration the demands of banking institutions before reducing the interest rates on small saving schemes
A reduction in interest rates on small saving schemes follow only after a reduction in repo rate by the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation:
The passage states that banking institutions had been demanding a reduction in small-saving interest rates for a year, and that the government finally announced such a reduction.
  • (a) The passage covers only one instance; ``whenever'' implies a universal rule — not inferable.
  • (b) The passage says the government brought rates on par with fixed deposits on this occasion; always maintaining parity is not stated.
  • (c) The word ``finally'' implies the government responded to banking institutions' demand after considering it. This directly supports: the government does sometimes take into consideration the demands of banking institutions before reducing small-saving interest rates. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) The passage does not state that a repo-rate cut is a necessary precondition; the reduction could happen independently.
\[\boxed{ \text{ C }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The nomenclature of Hindustani music has changed over the centuries. Since the medieval period dhrupad styles were identified as baanis. Terms like gayaki and baaj were used to refer to vocal and instrumental styles, respectively. With the institutionalization of music education the term gharana became acceptable. Gharana originally referred to hereditary musicians from a particular lineage, including disciples and grand disciples. Which one of the following pairings is NOT correct?
questions.explanation:
From the passage, the correct pairings are:
  • dhrupad style \(\leftrightarrow\) baani (style identifier in the medieval period).
  • gayaki \(\leftrightarrow\) vocal style.
  • baaj \(\leftrightarrow\) instrumental style (not ``institution'').
  • gharana \(\leftrightarrow\) lineage / hereditary musicians.
Checking the options:
  • (a) dhrupad, baani — correct pairing. (i.e. this one IS correct)
  • (b) gayaki, vocal — correct pairing.
  • (c) baaj, institution — INCORRECT; the passage pairs baaj with instrumental style, not institution. \(\checkmark\) (this is the NOT correct pair)
  • (d) gharana, lineage — correct pairing.
\[\boxed{\text{(C) } \textit{baaj}\text{, institution}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: "I read somewhere that in ancient times the prestige of a kingdom depended upon the number of taxes that it was able to levy on its people. It was very much like the prestige of a head-hunter in his own community." Based on the paragraph above, the prestige of a head-hunter depended upon __________
options: the number of taxes he could levy
the number of heads he could gather

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The strategies that the company ______ to sell its products ______ house-to-house marketing.
questions.explanation:
Blank 1 — subject is ``the company'' (singular, third person) \(\Rightarrow\) requires uses. Blank 2 — after ``products'', the connector must introduce an example without creating a second finite verb:
  • includes — third-person singular finite verb; creates a run-on with no clear subject.
  • include — bare plural finite verb; grammatically consistent with plural strategies as subject, making it a valid relative clause. \(\checkmark\)
Evaluating all options:
  • (A) use, includes — use fails third-person singular agreement with company.
  • (B) uses, include — uses correctly agrees with singular company; include correctly agrees with plural strategies in the relative clause ``… products [that] include house-to-house marketing''. \(\checkmark\)
  • (C) used, includes — past tense inappropriate for a general present-tense statement.
  • (D) uses, including — including is a participial preposition, not a finite verb; grammatically weaker than option (B) in this context.
\[\boxed{\text{(B) uses, include}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The boat arrived ______ dawn.
questions.explanation:
The correct preposition is determined by the temporal context:
  • ``in'' — used with a month (e.g. in June), a season (e.g. in winter), or a specific year (e.g. in 2019).
  • ``at'' — used with a particular time of day (e.g. at dawn) or a calendar festival season (e.g. at Christmas). \(\checkmark\)
  • ``on'' — used with a specific day of the week (e.g. on Thursday), a particular part of a date (e.g. on Sunday evening), or a specific date (e.g. on 9th March).
  • ``under'' — absurd in a temporal context; eliminated.
\[\boxed{\text{(B) at}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: When he did not come home, she ________ him lying dead on the roadside somewhere.
questions.explanation:
The sentence describes a woman imagining or forming a mental image of her missing partner lying dead by the roadside.
  • (a) concluded — implies a logical deduction, not a vivid mental image.
  • (b) looked — past tense of look; requires a direct object with a preposition (``looked at'') and implies physical sight.
  • (c) notice — implies physically seeing/observing something present; she was not at the roadside.
  • (d) pictured — means to form a mental image of someone or something; perfectly fits the context of imagining a scene in one's mind. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{(D) pictured}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
Four people are standing in a line facing you. They are Rahul, Mathew, Seema and Lohit. One is an engineer, one is a doctor, one a teacher and another a dancer. You are told that:
  1. Mathew is not standing next to Seema
  2. There are two people standing between Lohit and the engineer
  3. Rahul is not a doctor
  4. The teacher and the dancer are standing next to each other
  5. Seema is turning to her right to speak to the doctor standing next to her
Who among them is an engineer?
questions.explanation:
Four people face you in a line: their left is your right and vice versa. Constraints:
  1. Mathew is not next to Seema.
  2. There are two people between Lohit and the engineer.
  3. Rahul is not a doctor.
  4. The teacher and dancer are next to each other.
  5. Seema is turning right to speak to the doctor next to her.
From constraint 5: doctor is to Seema's right (which is our left in the facing view). From constraint 2: with 4 positions, Lohit and the engineer are at positions 1 and 4 (or 4 and 1), with two people between them. Applying all constraints, the only valid arrangement (from your left to right) is: \[\underbrace{\text{Lohit}}_{\text{Doctor}} \quad \text{Seema} \quad \text{Rahul} \quad \underbrace{\text{Mathew}}_{\text{Engineer}}\] Seema turns right (toward Lohit) to speak to the doctor \(\implies\) Lohit is the doctor (). Two people (Seema, Rahul) between Lohit and Mathew \(\implies\) Mathew is the engineer (). \[\boxed{\text{(D) Mathew}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: "Indian history was written by British historians -- extremely well documented and researched, but not always impartial. History had to serve its purpose: Everything was made subservient to the glory of the Union Jack. Latter-day Indian scholars presented a contrary picture." From the text above, we can infer that: Indian history written by British historians _______
options: was well documented and not researched but was always biased
was not well documented and researched and was always biased
was well documented and researched but was sometimes biased
was not well documented and researched and was sometimes biased
questions.explanation:
The passage states that Indian history written by British historians was ``extremely well documented and researched, but not always impartial''.
  • (a) ``Not always researched'' contradicts ``extremely well … researched''; and ``always biased'' is stronger than ``not always impartial''.
  • (b) ``Not well documented'' and ``always biased'' both contradict the passage.
  • (c) Well documented and researched ( from ``extremely well documented'') but sometimes biased ( from ``not always impartial''). Both halves directly supported. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) ``Not well documented'' directly contradicts the passage.
\[\boxed{ \text {C) was well documented and researched but was some- times biased}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: I am not sure if the bus that has been booked will be able to ______ all the students.
questions.explanation:
The sentence expresses uncertainty about whether the booked bus has sufficient capacity for all students.
  • (a) sit — too informal and does not convey sufficient space for all passengers.
  • (b) deteriorate — means to worsen over time; does not fit the capacity context.
  • (c) fill — implies making full, not providing room for someone.
  • (d) accommodate — means to provide sufficient space or room for; fits perfectly. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{D) accommodate}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The passengers were angry ______ the airline staff about the delay.
questions.explanation:
The correct collocation is ``angry with'' when the object of anger is a person or group of people.
  • (a) on — no standard collocation with angry.
  • (b) about — ``angry about'' is used with a situation or thing (e.g. angry about the delay), not with a person.
  • (c) with — ``angry with [a person/group]'' is the correct standard collocation. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) towards — expresses direction or attitude, not the standard collocation with angry.
\[\boxed{\text{C) with}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: It takes two hours for a person X to mow the lawn. Y can mow the same lawn in four hours. How long (in minutes) will it take X and Y, if they work together to mow the lawn?

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Newspapers are a constant source of delight and recreation for me. The ____ trouble is that I read ____ many of them.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires:
  • Blank 1: a word that restricts/qualifies ``trouble'' to convey that this is the sole drawback — ``only''.
  • Blank 2: an intensifier before ``many'' to signal excess — ``too''.
  • (a) even, quite — ``even trouble'' is grammatically awkward and ``quite many'' is non-standard.
  • (b) even too — ungrammatical as a pair.
  • (c) only, quite — ``quite many'' is non-standard; quite does not intensify many in this context.
  • (d) only, too — ``The only trouble is that I read too many of them.'' Standard, idiomatic English. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{D) only,too}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: An award-winning study by a group of researchers suggests that men are as prone to buying on impulse as women but women feel more guilty about shopping. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given text?
options: Some men and women indulge in buying on impulse
All men and women indulge in buying on impulse
Few men and women indulge in buying on impulse
Many men and women indulge in buying on impulse
questions.explanation:
The passage states men are ``as prone to buying on impulse as women''. This confirms that both men and women do buy on impulse — but the word ``prone'' (inclined/likely) does not assert that all or many do so; it only confirms that some do.
  • (a) Some — since both men and women are prone to impulse buying, at least some of each group buy on impulse. \(\checkmark\)
  • (b) All — ``all'' is too absolute; the passage does not guarantee every person buys on impulse.
  • (d) Few — contradicts the research finding that both groups are prone to it.
  • (b) Many — stronger than what the passage supports; prone only implies a tendency, not a large proportion.
\[\boxed{\text{A) Some men and women buy in impulse}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
Consider five people -- Mita, Ganga, Rekha, Lakshmi and Sana. Ganga is taller than both Rekha and Lakshmi. Lakshmi is taller than Sana. Mita is taller than Ganga. Which of the following conclusions are true?
  1. Lakshmi is taller than Rekha
  2. Rekha is shorter than Mita
  3. Rekha is taller than Sana
  4. Sana is shorter than Ganga
questions.explanation:
From the given statements, establish the height ordering: \[\text{Mita} > \text{Ganga} > \text{Rekha},\;\text{Lakshmi} > \text{Sana}\] Combined ordering: \[\text{Mita} > \text{Ganga} > \text{Rekha} \quad\text{and}\quad \text{Mita} > \text{Ganga} > \text{Lakshmi} > \text{Sana}\] Note: The relative order of Rekha and Sana cannot be determined. Evaluating the four conclusions:
  1. Lakshmi is taller than Rekha — cannot be confirmed (no direct comparison given).
  2. Rekha is shorter than Mita — TRUE (Mita \(>\) Ganga \(>\) Rekha). \(\checkmark\)
  3. Rekha is taller than Sana — cannot be determined from the given data.
  4. Sana is shorter than Ganga — TRUE (Ganga \(>\) Lakshmi \(>\) Sana). \(\checkmark\)
Both conclusions 2 and 4 are true: \[\boxed{\text{C) 2 and 4}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The lecture was attended by quite ______ students, so the hall was not very ______.
questions.explanation:
• Blank 1: ``quite ____ students'' — ``a few'' means a fairly large number (positive connotation), fitting the context of a lecture that was well-attended.
  • Blank 2: ``hall was not very ____'' — ``quiet'' means making little or no noise; a large crowd would make the hall noisy, hence not very quiet.
\[\boxed{\text{C) a few, quiet}}\]
Key points
  • ``A few'' \(=\) a fairly large number (positive); ``few'' \(=\) not many (negative/insufficient).
  • ``Quiet'' \(=\) making little noise; ``quite'' \(=\) fairly/somewhat — these homophones are frequent exam traps.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: They have come a long way in ________ trust among the users.
questions.explanation:
The phrase ``come a long way in ____'' requires a gerund (verb \(+\) -ing) as the object of the preposition in.
  • (a) Creating — gerund form; grammatically correct after the preposition in. \(\checkmark\)
  • (b) Created — past tense/past participle; cannot follow a preposition directly.
  • (c) Creation — a noun; while prepositionally permissible, ``come a long way in creating'' is the idiomatic standard.
  • (d) Create — base form; cannot follow a preposition.
\[\boxed{\text{A) Creating}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The CEO's decision to quit was as shocking to the Board as it was to _____.
questions.explanation:
The blank is the object of the preposition to in the comparative structure ``as shocking to the Board as it was to ____''. The pronoun must be in the objective case.
  • (a) I — subjective case; cannot be the object of a preposition.
  • (b) me — objective case; correct object of the preposition to. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) my — possessive adjective; cannot stand alone as the object of a preposition.
  • (d) myself — reflexive pronoun; used only when the subject and object refer to the same person within the clause.
\[\boxed{\text{B) me}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: "The increasing interest in tribal characters might be a mere coincidence, but the timing is of interest. None of this, though, is to say that the tribal hero has arrived in Hindi cinema, or that the new crop of characters represents the acceptance of the tribal character in the industry. The films and characters are too few to be described as a pattern." What does the word `arrived' mean in the paragraph above?
questions.explanation:
The word ``arrived'' in ``the tribal hero has arrived in Hindi cinema'' is used in its idiomatic sense: to gain recognition, acceptance, or a distinguished position in a domain.
  • (a) reached a terminus — physical travel; not idiomatic.
  • (b) came to a conclusion — refers to a logical endpoint, not a person's status.
  • (c) attained a status — matches the idiomatic meaning of ``arrived'' in this context. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) went to a place — physical movement; not idiomatic.
\[\boxed{\text{C) attained a status }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T are related and belong to the same family. P is the brother of S. Q is the wife of P. R and T are the children of the siblings P and S respectively. Which one of the following statements is necessarily FALSE?
options: S is the aunt of R
S is the aunt of T
S is the sister-in-law of Q
S is the brother of P
questions.explanation:
Given facts:
  • P is the brother of S \(\Rightarrow\) P is male.
  • Q is the wife of P \(\Rightarrow\) Q is female; P is male.
  • R is the child of P's sibling \(\Rightarrow\) R is the child of P.
  • T is the child of S's sibling \(\Rightarrow\) T is the child of S.
Evaluate each statement about S:
  • (a) S is the aunt of R — R is P's child, and S is P's sibling, so S is R's aunt if S is female (or R's uncle if S is male). Since S's gender is not fixed, this is possible. Not necessarily false.
  • (b) S is the aunt of T — T is S's own child, not S's niece/nephew. A parent can never simultaneously be their own child's aunt, regardless of S's gender. The statement ``S is the aunt of T'' is necessarily FALSE, since the parent–child relationship between S and T structurally excludes the aunt relationship, independent of S's gender. \(\checkmark\) necessarily false.
  • (c) S is the sister-in-law of Q — S is the sibling of Q's husband P; S could be male (brother-in-law) or female (sister-in-law). Possible.
  • (d) S is the brother of P — S is P's sibling; S's gender is unspecified, so S may be the brother. Possible.
\[\boxed{\text{B) S is the aunt of T }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Hima Das was ____ only Indian athlete to win ____ gold for India.
questions.explanation:
• Blank 1: ``____ only Indian athlete'' — ``the'' is required before a superlative/unique noun phrase (``the only'').
  • Blank 2: ``to win ____ gold'' — ``a'' is required as an indefinite article before a singular countable noun (one gold medal among many possible medals).
  • (a) the, many — ``many'' is a quantifier, not an article; grammatically inconsistent.
  • (b) the, a — both blanks correctly filled. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) an, a — ``an only'' is ungrammatical.
  • (d) an, the — ``an only'' ungrammatical; ``the gold'' implies a specific gold already mentioned.
\[\boxed{\text{B) the,a}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The Newspaper reports that over 500 hectares of tribal land spread across 28 tribal settlements in Mohimitampuram forest division have already been ``alienated''. A top forest official said, ``First the tribals are duped out of their land holdings. Second, the families thus rendered landless are often forced to encroach further into the forests''. On the basis of the information available in the paragraph, _____ is/are responsible for duping the tribals.
questions.explanation:
The passage contains two key facts:
  1. The Newspaper is only reporting the land alienation — it is not the agent responsible for duping the tribals.
  2. A top forest official made a statement about tribals being duped — this does not make the official the perpetrator; the statement is descriptive, not confessional.
Since neither the Newspaper nor the forest officials can be identified as responsible for duping based on the passage, and landless families are described as victims (forced to encroach), the passage provides insufficient information to identify the responsible party. \[\boxed{\text{D) it cannot be inferred who}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: "Popular Hindi fiction, despite -- or perhaps because of -- its wide reach, often does not appear in our cinema. As ideals that viewers are meant to look up to rather than identify with, Hindi film protagonists usually read books of aspirational value: textbooks, English books, or high value literature." Which one of the following CANNOT be inferred from the paragraph above?
options: Though popular Hindi fiction has wide reach, it often does not appear in the movies
Protagonists in Hindi movies, being ideals for viewers, read only books of aspirational value
Textbooks, English books or high literature have aspirational value, but not popular Hindi fiction
People do not look up to writers of textbooks, English books, or high value literature
questions.explanation:
The passage states that popular Hindi fiction ``does not appear in our cinema'' and that Hindi film protagonists read books of aspirational value ``as ideals that viewers are meant to look up to rather than identify with''. Evaluating each option:
  • (A) Though popular Hindi fiction has wide reach, it often does not appear in the movies --- directly stated in the passage. Can be inferred.
  • (B) Protagonists in Hindi movies, being ideals for viewers, read only books of aspirational value --- the word ``only'' makes this too absolute; the passage says protagonists usually read such books, not exclusively. Cannot be inferred. \(\checkmark\)
  • (C) Textbooks, English books or high literature have aspirational value, but not popular Hindi fiction --- implied by the contrast in the passage. Can be inferred.
  • (D) People do not look up to writers of textbooks, English books or high value literature --- the passage says viewers look up to protagonists who read such books, not to the writers of those books. This is a new claim not supported by the passage. Cannot be inferred. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{B) {Protagonists in Hindi movies, being ideals for viewers, read only books of aspirational value } }}\] \[\boxed{\text{OR}}\] \[\boxed{\text{D) {People do not look up to writers of textbooks, English books or high value literature } }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A worker noticed that the hour hand on the factory clock had moved by 225 degrees during her stay at the factory. For how long did she stay in the factory?
questions.explanation: We know that the hour hand completes one full rotation (\(360^{\circ}\)) in \(12\,\text{hours}\). So, for \(225^{\circ}\), the corresponding time is: \[t = \left(\frac{225}{360}\right) \times 12\] \[t = \frac{225 \times 12}{360} = \frac{2700}{360} = 7.5\,\text{hours}\] \[\boxed{{d)  7.5\,\text{hours}}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A firm hires employees at five different skill levels P, Q, R, S, T. The shares of employment at these skill levels of total employment in 2010 is given in the pie chart as shown. There were a total of 600 employees in 2010 and the total employment increased by 15% from 2010 to 2016. The total employment at skill levels P, Q and R remained unchanged during this period. If the employment at skill level S increased by 40% from 2010 to 2016, how many employees were there at skill level T in 2016?
questions.explanation:
In 2010, total employees \(= 600\). In 2016, there is 15% increment in number of employees. In 2016, total employees \(= 1.15 \times 600 = 690\). Given, there is no change in \(P\), \(Q\) and \(R\) type employees. There is 40% increment in \(S\) type employees. \[\text{Total } S\text{-type employees in 2016} =
    \left(600 \times \frac{25}{100}\right) \times 1.4 = 150 \times 1.4 = 210\] \[\text{Increase in } S\text{-type employees} =
    210 - \left(600 \times \frac{25}{100}\right) = 210 - 150 = 60\] \[\text{Initially, } T\text{-type employees} =
    \frac{5}{100} \times 600 = 30\] \[\text{In 2016, increase in } T\text{-type employees} =
    690 - 600 - 60 = 30\] \[\text{In 2016, total } T\text{-type employees} = 30 + 30 = 60\] \[\boxed{\text{C) } 60 \text{ employees}}\]

questions.question: If IMHO \(=\) JNIP; IDK \(=\) JEL; and SO \(=\) TP, then IDC \(=\) .
questions.explanation: Each letter in the code is obtained by incrementing the corresponding letter of the original word by \(+1\) position in the alphabet. Verify the given mappings: \[\text{IMHO} \xrightarrow{+1,+1,+1,+1} \text{JNIP}\] \[\text{IDK} \xrightarrow{+1,+1,+1} \text{JEL}\] \[\text{SO} \xrightarrow{+1,+1} \text{TP}\] Apply the same rule to IDC: \[\text{I} \to \text{J}, \quad \text{D} \to \text{E}, \quad \text{C} \to \text{D}\] \[\text{IDC} \xrightarrow{+1,+1,+1} \text{JED}\] \[\boxed{\text{(B) JED }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The product of three integers X, Y and Z is 192. Z is equal to 4 and P is equal to the average of X and Y. What is the minimum possible value of P?
questions.note: Marks awarded to all (official key: MTA)
questions.explanation: Given: \[X \times Y \times Z = 192, \qquad Z = 4\] \[X \times Y = \frac{192}{4} = 48\] Integer factor pairs of 48: \[48 = 1\times48 = 2\times24 = 3\times16 = 4\times12 = 6\times8\] \(P\) is the average of \(X\) and \(Y\): \[P = \frac{X + Y}{2}\] To minimise \(P\), minimise \(X+Y\). Among all factor pairs, \(6+8=14\) is the smallest sum: \[P_{\min} = \frac{6 + 8}{2} = \frac{14}{2} = 7\] \[\boxed { \text{(MTA) }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Fiscal deficit was 4% of the GDP in 2015 and that increased to 5% in 2016. If the GDP increased by 10% from 2015 to 2016, the percentage increase in the actual fiscal deficit is _____.
questions.explanation:
Let GDP in 2015 \(= 100\) (assumed base). \[\text{GDP in 2016} = 100 + 10\% \times 100 = 110\] \[\text{Deficit in 2015} = 4\%\ \text{of}\ 100 = 4\] \[\text{Deficit in 2016} = 5\%\ \text{of}\ 110 = 5.5\] Percentage increase in fiscal deficit: \[\frac{5.5 - 4}{4} \times 100 = \frac{1.5}{4} \times 100 = 37.5\,\%\] \[\boxed{{\text A )37.5}}\]
Key points
  • The deficit is expressed as a percentage of GDP, so an increase in GDP automatically raises the absolute deficit even if the deficit-to-GDP ratio changes only slightly.
  • Percentage increase in deficit \(= \dfrac{\text{New Deficit} - \text{Old Deficit}}{\text{Old Deficit}} \times 100\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not directly subtract the deficit percentages (\(5\% - 4\% = 1\%\)) without first converting them to absolute values on the respective GDP bases.
  • The GDP base in 2016 is 110, not 100 — failing to apply the GDP growth leads to an incorrect deficit figure.

questions.question: The expenditure on the project _____ as follows: equipment Rs.20 lakhs, salaries Rs.12 lakhs, and contingency Rs.3 lakhs.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires a verb that means to divide a total amount into its separate parts/components (the project expenditure is being itemised into equipment, salaries, and contingency).
  • (a) break down — base form; incorrect subject-verb agreement with the singular subject ``expenditure''.
  • (b) break — a noun or base verb; does not fit grammatically as a standalone verb here.
  • (c) breaks down — transitive phrasal verb meaning to divide a total into constituent parts. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) breaks — intransitive use of ``break''; does not carry the required meaning of itemisation.
\[\boxed {\text{C) breaks down}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Two cars start at the same time from the same location and go in the same direction. The speed of the first car is 50 km/h and the speed of the second car is 60 km/h. The number of hours it takes for the distance between the two cars to be 20 km is _____.
questions.explanation:
Both cars travel in the same direction, so the relative speed is the difference of their speeds. \[v_{A} = 50\,\text{km/h}, \qquad v_{B} = 60\,\text{km/h}\] \[v_{\text{rel}} = v_{B} - v_{A} = 60 - 50 = 10\,\text{km/h}\] \[\text{Required separation} = 20\,\text{km}\] \[\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{v_{\text{rel}}} = \frac{20}{10} = 2\,\text{hrs}\] \[\boxed{ \text{ B) 2}}\]
Key points
  • Same direction: Relative speed \(= v_{\text{faster}} - v_{\text{slower}}\).
  • Opposite directions: Relative speed \(= v_1 + v_2\).
  • Time to achieve a given separation \(= \dfrac{\text{Separation}}{\text{Relative Speed}}\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not use the sum of speeds; that applies only when the two objects move in opposite directions.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Ten friends planned to share equally the cost of buying a gift for their teacher. When two of them decided not to contribute, each of the other friends had to pay Rs 150 more. The cost of the gift was Rs. _____.
questions.explanation: Let the original equal share per friend \(= x\) (in Rs.). \[\text{Total cost of gift} = 10x\] When 2 friends drop out, the remaining 8 friends share the same total cost, each paying Rs.,150 more: \[8(x + 150) = 10x\] \[8x + 1200 = 10x\] \[2x = 1200 \implies x = 600\] \[\text{Total cost} = 10 \times 600 = \text{Rs.}\;6000\] \[\boxed{ \text{ C) 6000}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: In the given diagram, teachers are represented in the triangle, researchers in the circle and administrators in the rectangle. Out of the total number of the people, the percentage of administrators shall be in the range of ______.
questions.explanation: From the diagram, read the exclusive region values for each category: \[\text{Teachers only} = 70, \quad \text{Teachers} \cap \text{Administrators only} = 10, \quad \text{Administrators only} = 20\] \[\text{Administrators} \cap \text{Researchers only} = 20, \quad \text{Researchers only} = 40\] Total number of people: \[\text{Total} = 70 + 10 + 20 + 20 + 40 = 160\] Total administrators (all regions of the rectangle): \[\text{Administrators} = 10 + 20 + 20 = 50\] Percentage of administrators: \[\frac{\text{Administrators}}{\text{Total}} \times 100 = \frac{50}{160} \times 100 = 31.25\,\%\] \[\boxed{\text{C )31 to 45}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: In a college, there are three student clubs. Sixty students are only in the Drama club, 80 students are only in the Dance club, 30 students are only in the Maths club, 40 students are in both Drama and Dance clubs, 12 students are in both Dance and Maths clubs, 7 students are in both Drama and Maths clubs, and 2 students are in all the clubs. If 75% of the students in the college are not in any of these clubs, then the total number of students in the college is
questions.explanation:
Using the given data, the regions of the three-set Venn diagram are filled as follows (all values in number of students): \[\text{Only Drama} = 60, \quad \text{Only Dance} = 80, \quad \text{Only Maths} = 30\] \[\text{Drama} \cap \text{Dance only} = 40 - 2 - 5 - \ldots\] Applying inclusion-exclusion to recover the exclusive pairwise regions:
  • All three clubs: \(= 2\)
  • Drama \(\cap\) Dance (excluding all three) \(= 40 - 2 = 38\)
  • Dance \(\cap\) Maths (excluding all three) \(= 12 - 2 = 10\)
  • Drama \(\cap\) Maths (excluding all three) \(= 7 - 2 = 5\)
Total students in at least one club: \[N_{\text{clubs}} = 60 + 80 + 30 + 38 + 5 + 10 + 2 = 225\] Since \(75\%\) of the college students are not in any club, the students in clubs represent the remaining \(25\%\): \[25\% \text{ of Total} = 225\] \[\text{Total} = \frac{225}{25} \times 100 = 900\] \[\boxed{ \text{ C) 900}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The radius as well as the height of a circular cone increases by 10%. The percentage increase in its volume is_____.
questions.explanation:
Volume of a right circular cone: \[V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h\] Original volume: \[V_{0} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r_{1}^{2} h_{1} \tag{i}\] After a \(10\%\) increase in both radius and height: \[r_{\text{new}} = 1.1\,r_{1}, \qquad h_{\text{new}} = 1.1\,h_{1}\] \[V_{n} = \frac{1}{3}\pi (1.1\,r_{1})^{2}(1.1\,h_{1}) = \frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot 1.21\,r_{1}^{2} \cdot 1.1\,h_{1}\] \[V_{n} = 1.331 \left(\frac{1}{3}\pi r_{1}^{2} h_{1}\right) = 1.331\,V_{0}\] Percentage increase in volume: \[\%\;\Delta V = \frac{V_{n} - V_{0}}{V_{0}} \times 100 = \frac{1.331\,V_{0} - V_{0}}{V_{0}} \times 100 = 0.331 \times 100 = 33.1\,\%\] \[\boxed{ \text{ C) 33.1}}\]
Key points
  • \(V_{\text{cone}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h\); radius appears squared, so a \(10\%\) increase in \(r\) contributes a factor of \(1.1^{2} = 1.21\), not \(1.10\).
  • Combined scaling factor \(= 1.1^{2} \times 1.1 = 1.1^{3} = 1.331\).
  • % change \(= (k - 1) \times 100\) where \(k\) is the new-to-old ratio.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not add the percentage increases directly (\(10 + 10 + 10 = 30\%\)); compounding gives \(33.1\%\), not \(30\%\).
  • Remember \(r\) is squared in the formula — it contributes \((1.1)^{2}\), not \((1.1)^{1}\).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Five different books (P, Q, R, S, T) are to be arranged on a shelf. The books R and S are to be arranged first and second, respectively from the right side of the shelf. The number of different orders in which P, Q and T may be arranged is ______.
questions.explanation: Books R and S are fixed in the 1st and 2nd positions from the right of the shelf respectively: \[\underbrace{\text{P or Q or T}}_{\text{pos 1}} \quad \underbrace{\text{P or Q or T}}_{\text{pos 2}} \quad \underbrace{\text{P or Q or T}}_{\text{pos 3}} \quad \underbrace{\text{S}}_{\text{pos 4 (fixed)}} \quad \underbrace{\text{R}}_{\text{pos 5 (fixed)}}\] The remaining three books P, Q, T can be arranged freely in the three remaining positions: \[{}^{3}P_{3} = 3! = 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6\] \[\boxed{ \text {B) 6}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The bar graph in Panel (a) shows the proportion of male and female illiterates in 2001 and 2011. The proportions of males and females in 2001 and 2011 are given in Panel (b) and (c), respectively. The total population did not change during this period. The percentage increase in the total number of literates from 2001 to 2011 is _____.
questions.explanation: Let total population in both 2001 and 2011 \(= 100\) (same, as given). In 2001: Males \(= 60\), Females \(= 40\). \[\text{Male illiterates} = 50\% \times 60 = 30\] \[\text{Female illiterates} = 60\% \times 40 = 24\] \[\text{Total illiterates in 2001} = 30 + 24 = 54 \implies \text{Literates in 2001} = 100 - 54 = 46\] In 2011: Males \(= 50\), Females \(= 50\). \[\text{Male illiterates} = 40\% \times 50 = 20\] \[\text{Female illiterates} = 40\% \times 50 = 20\] \[\text{Total illiterates in 2011} = 20 + 20 = 40 \implies \text{Literates in 2011} = 100 - 40 = 60\] Percentage increase in literates from 2001 to 2011: \[\frac{60 - 46}{46} \times 100 = \frac{14}{46} \times 100 \approx 30.43\,\%\] \[\boxed{ \text {A) 30.43}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Five people P, Q, R, S and T work in a bank. P and Q don't like each other but have to share an office till T gets a promotion and moves to the big office next to the garden. R, who is currently sharing an office with T wants to move to the adjacent office with S, the handsome new intern. Given the floor plan, what is the current location of Q, R and T? (\(\text{O} = \text{Office}\), \(\text{WR} = \text{Washroom}\))
questions.explanation:
Constraints extracted from the problem:
  1. P and Q must share one office (forced by management until T gets promoted).
  2. T wants to move to the office adjacent to S's office.
  3. R currently shares with T and wants to move to the adjacent office with S.
  4. After T moves next to garden (big office), R and S share an office.
Evaluating options:
  • (a) P alone in O1, Q alone in O2 — P and Q not sharing; violates constraint 1.
  • (b) P,Q in O1; T in O3; R,S in O4 — R and T are not adjacent to S; violates the adjacency requirement.
  • (c) P,Q in O1; R,T in O3; S in O4 — P and Q share (); R and T share, with S in the adjacent office (); layout consistent with all constraints. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) P,Q in O1; R in O3; S in O4; T in Manager's room — T moving to manager's room is not described; inconsistent.
\[\boxed{\text{(C)}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The missing number in the given sequence 343, 1331, ____, 4913 is
questions.explanation:
Identify the pattern in the series \(343,\;1331,\;\_\_,\;4913\): \[343  = 7^{3}, \qquad
    1331 = 11^{3}, \qquad
    4913 = 17^{3}\] The bases are consecutive prime numbers: \(7,\;11,\;13,\;17,\;\ldots\) Missing term corresponds to the prime \(13\): \[13^{3} = 2197\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 2197}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: How many integers are there between 100 and 1000 all of whose digits are even?
questions.explanation:
We need 3-digit integers (100 to 999) where every digit is even. Even digits available: \(\{0,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) — five choices.
  • Hundreds digit: cannot be 0 (else the number \(< 100\)). Choices: \(\{2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) \(= 4\) options.
  • Tens digit: any even digit including 0. Choices: \(\{0,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) \(= 5\) options.
  • Units digit: any even digit including 0. Choices: \(\{0,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) \(= 5\) options.
\[\text{Total} = 4 \times 5 \times 5 = 100\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 100}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The ratio of the number of boys and girls who participated in an examination is 4:3. The total percentage of candidates who passed the examination is 80 and the percentage of girls who passed is 90. The percentage of boys who passed is ______.
questions.explanation:
Let number of boys \(= 4x\) and number of girls \(= 3x\), so total students \(= 7x\). Total students who passed (80% of total): \[\frac{80}{100} \times 7x = 5.6x\] Girls who passed (90% of girls): \[\frac{90}{100} \times 3x = 2.7x\] Boys who passed:
\[5.6x - 2.7x = 2.9x\] Percentage of boys who passed (out of total boys \(= 4x\)): \[\frac{2.9x}{4x} \times 100 = \frac{2.9}{4} \times 100 = 72.50\,\%\] \[\boxed{\text{B) 72.50}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Given two sets \(X = \{1, 2, 3\}\) and \(Y = \{2, 3, 4\}\), we construct a set Z of all possible fractions where the numerators belong to set X and the denominators belong to set Y. The product of elements having minimum and maximum values in the set Z is ______.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: On a horizontal ground, the base of a straight ladder is 6 m away from the base of a vertical pole. The ladder makes an angle of 45 to the horizontal. If the ladder is resting at a point located at one-fifth of the height of the pole from the bottom, the height of the pole is ____ meters.
questions.explanation:
The ladder makes \(45^{\circ}\) with the horizontal ground. The base of the ladder is \(6\,\text{m}\) from the pole. The ladder rests at a point that is \(\tfrac{1}{5}\) of the pole's height \(H\) from the bottom. \[\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\] The ladder meets the pole at height \(\dfrac{H}{5}\), and the horizontal distance is \(6\,\text{m}\): \[\tan 45^{\circ} = \frac{H/5}{6} = 1\] \[\frac{H}{5} = 6 \implies H = 30\,\text{m}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 30}}\]
Key points
  • \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\); the opposite side here is the height at which the ladder rests (\(H/5\)), not the full pole height \(H\).
  • \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\), so opposite \(=\) adjacent \(\implies \dfrac{H}{5} = 6 \implies H = 30\,\text{m}\).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: If E = 10; J = 20; O = 30; and T = 40, what will be P + E + S + T?
questions.explanation: Each letter is assigned its positional value in the alphabet. Using the given key: \(E=10,\;J=20,\;O=30,\;T=40\), the pattern is that each letter's value equals its position multiplied by a constant. Decoding the remaining letters: \[P = 32,\quad E = 10,\quad S = 38,\quad T = 40\] \[P + E + S + T = 32 + 10 + 38 + 40 = 120\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 120}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The new cotton technology, Bollgard-II, with herbicide tolerant traits has developed into a thriving business in India. However, the commercial use of this technology is not legal in India. Notwithstanding that, reports indicate that the herbicide tolerant Bt cotton had been purchased by farmers at an average of Rs 200 more than the control price of ordinary cotton, and planted in 15% of the cotton growing area in the 2017 Kharif season. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?
options: Farmers want to access the new technology if India benefits from it
Farmers want to access the new technology even if it is not legal
Farmers want to access the new technology for experimental purposes
Farmers want to access the new technology by paying high price
questions.explanation:
The passage states that despite the commercial use of Bollgard-II being illegal in India, farmers purchased it in significant quantities (15% of the cotton-growing area in the 2017 Kharif season), paying a premium of Rs,200 more than control-price cotton.
  • (a) Only if India benefits — the passage shows farmers acted regardless of national policy benefit.
  • (b) Even if not legal — the passage emphasises widespread adoption despite illegality; farmers paid extra to access the technology illegally. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) Experimental purposes — the scale of adoption (15% of area) suggests commercial, not experimental, use.
  • (d) By paying high price — partial truth; price detail is secondary to the core inference about illegality.
\[\boxed{\text{B) Farmers want to access the new technology even if it is not legal}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: In a sports academy of 300 people, 105 play only cricket, 70 play only hockey, 50 play only football, 25 play both cricket and hockey, 15 play both hockey and football and 30 play both cricket and football. The rest of them play all three sports. What is the percentage of people who play at least two sports?
questions.explanation:
Given data for 300 people in a sports academy: \[\text{Only Cricket} = 105,\quad \text{Only Hockey} = 70,\quad \text{Only Football} = 50\] \[\text{Cricket} \cap \text{Hockey only} = 25,\quad \text{Hockey} \cap \text{Football only} = 15,\quad \text{Cricket} \cap \text{Football only} = 30\] Total accounted for in exactly-one and exactly-two categories: \[105 + 70 + 50 + 25 + 15 + 30 = 295\] Players in all three sports: \[300 - 295 = 5\] Players playing at least 2 sports (exactly two \(+\) all three): \[25 + 30 + 15 + 5 = 75\] Percentage: \[\frac{75}{300} \times 100 = 25\,\%\] \[\boxed{\text{B) 25.00}}\]
Key points
  • ``At least 2 sports'' \(=\) (exactly 2 sports) \(+\) (all 3 sports).
  • Find the all-three region by subtracting the sum of all other exclusive regions from the total.
Mistakes to avoid
  • The pairwise intersection values given (25, 15, 30) are exclusive pairwise regions (not including the all-three overlap); do not subtract the all-three count again.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A square has sides 5 cm smaller than the sides of a second square. The area of the larger square is four times the area of the smaller square. The side of the larger square is ___ cm.
questions.explanation:
Let the side of the larger square \(= x\,\text{cm}\). \[\text{Side of smaller square} = (x - 5)\,\text{cm}\] \[\text{Area of larger square} = x^{2}, \qquad \text{Area of smaller square} = (x-5)^{2}\] Given condition — area of larger square is four times that of smaller: \[x^{2} = 4(x-5)^{2}\] \[x^{2} = 4(x^{2} - 10x + 25)\] \[x^{2} = 4x^{2} - 40x + 100\] \[3x^{2} - 40x + 100 = 0\] Taking the positive square root of both sides of \(x = 2(x-5)\) (since \(x > 0\) and \(x > 5\)): \[x = 2(x - 5) \implies x = 2x - 10 \implies x = 10\,\text{cm}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 10.00}}\]
Key points
  • \(x^{2} = 4(x-5)^{2}\) implies \(x = \pm\,2(x-5)\); take the positive root that satisfies \(x > 5\).
  • Verify: larger area \(= 100\), smaller area \(= 25\); \(100 = 4 \times 25\). \(\checkmark\)

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Daytime temperatures in Delhi can ______ 40 C.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires a verb that collocates naturally with a temperature value to indicate that temperatures attain a particular level.
  • (a) get — informal; ``get 40°C'' is non-standard.
  • (b) stand — used for static readings (``the temperature stands at''), not for attaining a maximum.
  • (c) reach — standard collocation: ``temperatures can reach 40°C'' is idiomatic and correct. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) peak — intransitive; cannot be followed directly by a temperature value without a preposition.
\[\boxed{\text{C) reach}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The growth rate of ABC Motors in 2017 was the same _____ XYZ Motors in 2016.
questions.explanation:
The sentence compares ``the growth rate of ABC Motors'' (singular noun phrase) with ``the growth rate of XYZ Motors''. The correct comparative structure requires a singular demonstrative pronoun ``that of'' to avoid repeating the noun phrase.
  • (a) as off — ungrammatical.
  • (b) as those of — ``those'' is plural; the subject
  • (c) as that off — ``off'' is incorrect (should be ``of''). (growth rate) is singular.
  • (d) as that of — ``that'' correctly substitutes the singular noun ``growth rate''; ``of'' completes the possessive. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{D) as that of}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Suresh wanted to lay a new carpet in his new mansion with an area of \(70 \times 55\) sq. mts. However an area of 550 sq. mts. had to be left out for flower pots. If the cost of carpet is Rs. 50 per sq. mts., how much money (in Rs.) will be spent by Suresh for the carpet now?
questions.explanation:
Total area of the mansion: \[70 \times 55 = 3850\,\text{sq.\,m}\] Area to be carpeted (subtracting flower-pot area): \[3850 - 550 = 3300\,\text{sq.\,m}\] Cost of carpet at Rs.,50 per sq.,m: \[3300 \times 50 = \text{Rs.}\;1{,}65{,}000\] \[\boxed{\text{A) Rs.\;1{,}65{,}000}}\]
Key points
  • Net carpeted area \(=\) Total area \(-\) Area left out.
  • Cost \(=\) Net area \(\times\) Rate per unit area.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A retaining wall with measurements \(30\,\text{m} \times 12\,\text{m} \times 6\,\text{m}\) was constructed with bricks of dimensions \(8\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm}\). If 60% of the wall consists of bricks, the number of bricks used for the construction is ____ lakhs.
questions.explanation:
Wall dimensions: \(30\,\text{m} \times 12\,\text{m} \times 6\,\text{m}\). Brick dimensions: \(8\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm}\). Bricks constitute \(60\%\) of the wall volume. Converting wall dimensions to cm and equating volumes: \[30 \times 12 \times 6 \times 10^{6}\,\text{cm}^{3} \times 0.6 = 8 \times 6 \times 6\,\text{cm}^{3} \times x\] \[x = \frac{30 \times 12 \times 6 \times 10^{6} \times 0.6}{8 \times 6 \times 6}\] \[x = 4.5 \times 10^{6} = 45 \times 10^{5} = 45\,\text{lakh bricks}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 45}}\]
Key points
  • Convert all dimensions to the same unit before equating volumes.
  • Number of bricks \(= \dfrac{\text{Wall volume} \times \text{brick fraction}}{\text{Volume of one brick}}\).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Mohan, the manager, wants his four workers to work in pairs. No pair should work for more than 5 hours. Ram and John have worked together for 5 hours. Krishna and Amir have worked as a team for 2 hours. Krishna does not want to work with Ram. Whom should Mohan allot to work with John, if he wants all the workers to continue working?
questions.explanation:
Constraints:
  • Ram and John have already worked together for 5 hours — their pair is complete (max 5 hours reached).
  • Krishna and Amir have worked together for 2 hours — 3 hours remain.
  • Krishna cannot work with Ram.
  • All four workers must continue working.
Since Ram--John are done and Krishna--Ram is forbidden, The new pairs must be formed from \(\{\text{John, Krishna, Ram, Amir}\}\): \[\text{New Pair 1: John and Krishna} \qquad \text{New Pair 2: Ram and Amir}\] John should be allotted to work with Krishna. \[\boxed{\text{B) Krishna}}\]
